First release of this Keychron K3 Max firmware. Compared with the stock Keychron K3 Max firmware 1.1.0
(Keychron `qmk_firmware`, branch `2025q3`):

## Code base

- Keychron 2025q3 is built on QMK `master` as of 2025-09-10. This firmware merges it with QMK `master` as of
  2026-11-15: 703 QMK commits, including the breaking-change cycles of 2025-11-30, 2026-02-22, 2026-05-31 and
  2026-08-30. Keychron's keyboard code (wireless, low power, indicators, raw HID) is kept and adapted to the
  upstream API (debounce signatures, removed GPIO aliases).
- Every submodule now comes from QMK. In particular ChibiOS is QMK's 21.11.x with the HAL 9.1 backports, instead
  of the Keychron fork (HAL 8.4). The three Keychron ChibiOS patches the K3 Max (STM32F401) needs are applied from
  the keyboard code (`keyboards/keychron/k3_max/chibios_fixes.c` and `hal_usb_lld.h`):
  - GPIOH is clocked, so the low power code can park H0/H1 before entering STOP mode.
  - The backup domain is unlocked and waited for before ChibiOS configures the RTC, which drives the wireless
    battery and indicator timers.
  - USB connect/disconnect leave VBUS sensing off: on the K3 Max PA9 is the Bluetooth mode switch, not VBUS.

## What the QMK update brings to the K3 Max

Only the upstream changes that touch features this keyboard uses are listed.

- **Waking the computer** (USB): the keys pressed to wake the host from sleep are no longer typed, so they do not
  end up as stray characters in the password prompt ([#23389](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/23389)).
- **Media and system keys**: the System Control usage range is restricted to the keys QMK actually sends, so
  Linux and Steam no longer detect the keyboard as a gamepad or joystick
  ([#26295](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26295)), while the sleep key keeps working on Windows
  ([#26455](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26455)).
- **Win Lock**: Keychron's Win Lock uses QMK's GUI toggle. While it is on, mod-tap and one-shot keys with
  right-hand modifiers (`RCTL`, `RSFT`, `RALT`) were turned into their left-hand counterparts; now only the GUI
  keys are blocked ([#25780](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/25780)).
- **Lighting effects**:
  - Reactive and splash effects (RGB and white): the key-hit tracker copied overlapping memory, which is
    undefined behaviour and with some compilers froze the keyboard after nine keystrokes
    ([#26306](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26306)).
  - Typing heatmap (RGB): pressing keys at one edge no longer lights up keys at the opposite edge
    ([#25915](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/25915)); it no longer reads out of bounds on matrix
    positions without an LED, and together with digital rain it honours keys mapped to more than one LED
    ([#26294](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26294)).
- **Mouse keys**: holding a mouse button key before moving no longer makes the cursor jump
  ([#25716](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/25716)), and mouse reports, horizontal wheel included,
  stay within the range declared in the USB descriptor
  ([#26195](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26195), [#26230](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26230)).
- **VIA**: the keyboard reports VIA protocol 13 instead of 12, which tells VIA which keycode list matches the
  firmware ([#26001](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26001)).
- **Custom keymaps**: Speculative Hold for mod-taps ([#25572](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/25572)),
  lighter tap dance state ([#25415](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/25415)), and fixes to single-key
  combos ([#25198](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/25198)), Repeat Key
  ([#25926](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/25926), [#26312](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26312)),
  retro tapping ([#26127](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26127)) and Key Lock
  ([#26269](https://github.com/qmk/qmk_firmware/pull/26269)).

## New: battery readout over raw HID, also in wireless mode

- Raw HID now works through the wireless link (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz), not only over USB. Keychron gated it behind
  `WILRESS_RAW_ENABLE`, which no board enabled, and neither of its two paths built: the VIA one called a function
  that does not exist (`via_raw_hid_receive`), the other one an undeclared `kc_raw_hid_rx`. Both now go to
  `raw_hid_receive`, like USB, so it works with and without VIA.
- New command `0xA7 0xF0` (Keychron misc group, battery query). The reply keeps the two command bytes and adds:

  | Byte | Content |
  |---|---|
  | 2 | `0` success, `1` failure (board without wireless) |
  | 3 | Battery level, percent |
  | 4–5 | Battery voltage in mV, little endian |
  | 6 | `0` not charging, `1` charging, `2` fully charged |
  | 7 | Transport: `1` USB, `2` Bluetooth, `4` 2.4 GHz |
  | 8 | Wireless state: `1` initialized, `2` disconnected, `3` connected, `4` pairing, `5` reconnecting, `6` suspended |
  | 9 | Reply layout version, currently `1` |

## New: release number in the firmware version

- The Keychron web tool shows the release number and the build date (`v0.0.1 <yyyy-mm-dd-hh:mm:ss>`) instead of
  `v1.1.0` and the build date, so it tells which release is flashed. Builds that are not a release report
  `dev-<commit>` (CI) or `dev` (local). The Keychron tool may offer the stock firmware as an update: installing it
  replaces this firmware.

## Fixes

- EEPROM emulation (wear leveling): a forced consolidation left the flash unlocked when its caller had not
  unlocked it, for example while replaying the write log at boot. It is now locked again on every path.
- ANSI RGB: `default_region` had 85 entries for 84 LEDs, which breaks the build under QMK's `-Werror`.
  The extra entry was a trailing zero, so the lighting regions do not change.
- Wireless indicators: `LED_PIN_ON_STATE` gets the same default as QMK core (`1`), so the white-backlight
  variants build without repeating the default value in `keyboard.json`.

## Unchanged

- Keymaps, layouts, lighting effects and the USB device version (1.1.0, ANSI 1.1.1), so over USB the board
  identifies itself exactly as the stock firmware does. The VIA definitions attached to this release are
  Keychron's, unchanged.
